main_text.l: VII. Deus est spiritus essentia vnus, perso-
nis & operibus trinus. Hoc theorema est funda-
mentum omnis solidæ sapientiæ: quia omnis sapientia
extra & citra hoc dogma est pura puta stultitia. Quod
quàm sit verum, non norunt nisi illi, qui vestigium vni-
tatis & trinitatis in totâ naturâ oculis mentis se ingerere
animaduerterunt. Percurre omnes & singulas creaturas,
videbis vnitatem non esse sine trinitate, neque trinitatem
sine vnitate. Placet intueri corporeas naturas? Vides
ibi corpus, spiritum & animam. In homine id est euidens.
1.Thes.5.v.23. In reliquis creaturis corporeis id euincit ra-
tio, quam comitatur experientia. Nihil iam dico de tri-
bus principiis, quæ distinctè constituunt vnum corpus.
Assurgamus ad animam rationalem & angelos, & dispi-
ciamus, quomodo ibi sit vnum & trinum. Tria ibi sunt
intimè vnita, videl. intellectus, voluntas, & potentia a-
gendi spiritualis. Præterea alia, quæ multa sunt. Neque
vero est, quòd aliquis criminetur hanc similitudinem,
quòd maxima ibi sit dissimilitudo. Nam paulò ante dixi,
vestigium duntaxat huius arcani cerni in naturâ, non
expressam similitudinem. Sed euoluamus theorema
nostrum. Principio vnitas essentia in Deo adeo est ma-
gna,

page.notes: Right margin numerals beside the lines are read as 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 but are partly cut off at the edge; the readings "2", "2", "5", "3" and "1" are doubtful and may be tens or other numerals. The word "est" after "Eum" in the VI paragraph is printed as such and is left as printed. The sentence "extra & citra hoc dogma est pura puta stultitia" looks heavier than the surrounding text and is marked as italic; it may be bold type. The word "essentia" in the VII heading is read as printed. The line "gna," at the lower right is the catchword. A small mark beneath it is not transcribed.
